column3: Pairs certainty with established truth, supporting certainty as an objective final reality as well as settled knowledge.
Sets rejected truth against accusations of madness; it frames how a truth can arrive yet be resisted before final certainty.
Describes destruction coming from an unperceived direction, a secondary parallel to certainty catching its subjects.
The visit to graves supplies a terminal, death-facing setting for the arrival named in 74:47.
Opens the surah's commission but does not itself clarify the arriving certainty.
Repeats the same until-certainty-arrives construction, making continuous worship before a terminal arrival a direct parallel.
Contrasts actionable certain knowledge with later confrontation, preserving a knowledge-reading alongside a terminal-reading.
Immediately states that intercession no longer benefits them after the certainty of 74:47.
Shows certainty operating before judgment through endurance and guidance, contrasting useful earlier certainty with final certainty.
Pairs certainty with truth, strengthening the reading of certainty as reality fully established rather than mere confidence.
Identifies those being questioned as the guilty, anchoring the speakers of 74:47 in the immediate scene.
Portrays punishment as an event that comes to wrongdoers and triggers futile requests for delay.
Distinguishes direct sight as certainty, preserving a face-to-face confirmation reading for 74:47.
Links certainty to recognizing lordship across the heavens, earth, and what lies between.
Opposes unsupported claims to a clear authority that must be brought, a secondary evidence-and-certainty parallel.
A temporary turning away until a time has little specific bearing on certainty's arrival.
Its warning commission is the earlier opportunity that the later confession in 74:47 closes.
The offered clear authority and threatened consequence preserve an evidentiary, not solely terminal, route to certainty.
Uses commanded coming in a creation scene, but does not connect that arrival to certainty or the guilty.
Places the questioning in gardens, clarifying the vantage from which the guilty explain their end.
Rejected truth later returns as unavoidable news, closely paralleling a dismissed reality that finally reaches them.
The just scales and accounting day give the judgment setting in which final certainty has consequence.
This exception concerning spouses does not add to the sense of 74:47.
Connects certainty about the hereafter with present worship and giving, contrasting it with the confessed failures nearby.
Makes separation contingent on a clear proof arriving, a parallel threshold of decisive disclosure.
Part of the opening commission, with only indirect relevance to the final confession.
A past report arriving to the hearer supports a secondary reading of arrival as conveyed news or warning.
Unending doubt lasts until the Hour or punishment suddenly comes, a close terminal parallel.
Sets apart the companions of the right, sharpening the contrast with the guilty speakers of 74:47.
Makes a historical report arrive as present warning; its destruction aspect is a secondary parallel only.
Names the praying as an exception, directly contrasting with the guilty admission in 74:43.
A threat of approach from every direction is only a broad verbal parallel to being reached.
Contrasts repeated demands for a sign with signs already made clear to people of certainty.
Guidance after determination is too general to explain the certainty in 74:47.
An opening purification command contrasts with the guilty group's retrospectively confessed path.
Shows signs repeatedly arriving and being turned from, an earlier stage before an unavoidable outcome.
Affirms that the recompense is bound to occur, supplying the certainty of the surrounding judgment horizon.
One of the speakers' confessed practices, directly contributing to the sequence ending in 74:47.
Links certainty to recognizing lordship over the heavens, earth, and their interval.
Truth is brought with a claim of truthfulness, supplying an arrival-of-truth parallel without the terminal force.
The right and left receivers may support accountability context but do not explain certainty's arrival.
Treats created life as signs for people who are certain, preserving a reflective knowledge reading.
Life, death, and return provide the death-and-return horizon for the certainty that came to the guilty.
The command to leave defilement contrasts with the guilty group's unreformed conduct.
Punishment or the Hour coming tests every claimed refuge, paralleling final certainty as crisis.
The oath by dawn does not add a clear connection to 74:47.
The refusal to feed the poor is another direct element in the confession before 74:47.
Demanding associates to appear exposes unsupported claims; it is a secondary arrival-and-proof parallel.
Records a demanded sacrificial proof and exposes refusal after such signs had already come.
The command about giving has only broad contextual relevance to the guilty confession.
Locates signs in the earth for those with certainty, retaining an evidential reading alongside terminal certainty.
Calls a report certain while also showing it is a claim brought by a messenger, not self-validating certainty.
Ends the surah with remembrance, reverence, and forgiveness, framing a contrary possibility to the guilty outcome.
Depicts guidance already come but belief deferred until prior punishment or visible punishment arrives.
Explicitly opposes conjecture and disputed appearance to certainty, illuminating certainty as more than assertion.
Waiting until a time in an accusation scene has only a loose temporal parallel.
A report of Moses arriving to the hearer offers a limited narrative-arrival parallel.
A maturity threshold and tested judgment are unrelated to the final certainty of 74:47.
The command to endure for the Lord is the commissioned alternative to the speakers' later failure.
Neglected signs leading to reciprocal abandonment parallels the consequence of ignored prior guidance.
Death ends a confinement, but the legal setting does not clarify certainty in 74:47.
Their demand for unrolled pages explains continued resistance to warning before the final arrival.
Describes the revelation as insight, guidance, and mercy for those certain, contrasting available guidance with the confession.
Its marital prohibition and faith condition have no specific connection to final certainty.
Calamity came upon destroyed towns at unsuspected times, paralleling an arriving consequence.
Names lack of certainty amid questions of creation and authority, preserving a cognitive reading.
A marital legal condition does not add to the meaning of 74:47.
The trumpet blast begins the immediate difficult-day sequence that culminates in the later testimony.
Certainty concerning the hereafter gives a prior, present orientation to the reality later encountered.
Knowledge and competing communal demands only loosely relate to certainty's arrival.
The denial of the Day of Recompense is the final stated practice immediately before 74:47.
The given book as guidance shows the earlier means of direction that precedes final accountability.
Awaiting God's command is a temporal parallel but not a clarification of certainty.
The garden prohibition does not add a clear connection to 74:47.
Grounds patience in God's true promise and contrasts it with those lacking certainty.
A historical trial after apparent success provides little direct help with final certainty.
Calls the trumpet day difficult, directly elaborating the event-horizon of 74:47.
Connects certainty with recognizing the excellence of divine judgment, an earlier evaluative counterpart to final judgment.
Its conflict condition has no specific bearing on the certainty that came.
The first direct confession, not being among those who prayed, begins the causal list completed by 74:47.
Punishment may arrive by night or day, reinforcing the inescapable arrival of consequence.
A condition for attaining righteousness is not a close parallel to 74:47.
Promises recompense for distortion of divine names, adding the certainty of eventual return for deeds.
Guidance that comes from God offers the prior path whose following averts fear and grief.
Demand for direct sight is answered by seizure, a cautionary parallel to confirmation arriving as consequence.
Specifies that the difficult day is not easy for disbelievers, directly continuing the terminal scene.
What is promised is coming and cannot be escaped, closely matching an event that reaches its subjects.
Certainty about the hereafter sustains prayer and giving, contrasting with the guilty confessions in 74:43-46.
An instruction to bring skilled magicians is a bare coming verb without relevant certainty.
A demand for angels as proof is recast by the surrounding response as a perilous arrival, preserving a secondary confirmation reading.
A life-stage threshold and gratitude do not directly clarify the certainty in 74:47.
Fearful giving before return to the Lord supplies a present ethical response to coming accountability.
The opening of a severe-punishment gate leaves its subjects despairing, a terminal-consequence parallel.
Calls the unseen promise something that is coming, directly supporting arrival as an active future reality.
A narrated encounter and objection have no specific connection to certainty's arrival.
Each person comes alone on the Resurrection Day, reinforcing the untransferable individual outcome after 74:47.
A challenge to bring proof is only a minimal verbal parallel.
Calls for return before punishment comes, after which help is unavailable; a close parallel to the closed interval in 74:47-48.
Deferred knowledge after ingratitude gives only a broad future-consequence parallel.
Joins the truth-founded creation with the certainly coming Hour, supporting both truth and terminal-arrival readings.
States that death reaches people wherever they are, a close parallel to certainty as an inescapable arrival.
The appointed death-messengers take souls without neglect, specifying the agency of a terminal arrival.
The death agonies and angels' demand for souls portray a compelled, irreversible encounter.
Shows signs being shown so that Abraham may be among the certain, preserving the evidentiary certainty reading.
The angels take the souls of the good and announce peace, supplying a contrary terminal outcome.
Makes every soul taste death and places life and death within a test before return.
When death comes, the plea to return marks the closure of the prior opportunity for action.
The barrier until resurrection confirms that the post-death state cannot be reversed by the speaker's request.
Pairs the universal tasting of death with return, directly supporting a death-and-account horizon.
Names the angel of death as the one who takes the hearers before their return to their Lord.
Describes souls being taken at death and during sleep, distinguishing final taking from a temporary analogue.
The agony of death comes with truth and confronts the person with what was evaded.
At the soul's reaching the throat, human power proves unable to avert the terminal event.
Declares that the death from which people flee will meet them, closely paralleling certainty coming to its subjects.
Once the appointed term comes, no delay is granted, clarifying the irreversible cutoff implied by 74:47.
The soul reaching the collarbone gives the bodily threshold of the terminal arrival.
The driving at that threshold is to the Lord, connecting death directly to final return.
